claim: Payload referencing increases user-perceived turn latency despite reducing token generation.
falsifier: Measure user-perceived turn latency with and without payload referencing in a multi-agent system on code-intensive tasks.

conditions: LLM-based agents (Claude 3.5 Sonnet supervisor, Claude 3.0 Sonnet specialists)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task domain, LLM models, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Payload referencing mechanism–user-perceived turn latency boundary

claim: Using object-centric grounding as visual chain-of-thought signals improves multimodal reasoning by enabling more effective goal-conditioned visual attention.
falsifier: One could test this by comparing a baseline MLLM without object-centric grounding against a version that incorporates such grounding on a visual reasoning benchmark, measuring accuracy and attention alignment.

conditions: the model includes a vision encoder and a language decoder
the grounding signals are generated as text-to-box predictions
the model is trained on datasets with region-of-interest annotations
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system (Argus framework), tasks (multimodal reasoning and referral object grounding), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond these is unestablished.

title: Incorporating object-centric grounding as–reasoning quality and more…
